groups.label: Look Back
items: Charlemagne was crowned emperor in Rome in 800. Add 82 years → 882: in the far east of Europe, another new power was taking shape around Kiev.

The Viking Age opened with the raid on Lindisfarne in 793. The Norse traders who sailed down Russia's rivers were part of the same wave; about ninety years later, one of their princes held Kiev → 882.

groups.label: Year of 882
items: Think 8-8-2: the 800s were the Vikings' century, and the two eights are the two cities Oleg joined, Novgorod in the north and Kiev in the south.

groups.label: Look Ahead
items: Prince Vladimir of Kiev converted to Christianity in 988, the famous 'Baptism of Rus'. Subtract about a century (106 years) → 882, when Kiev first became the Rus capital.
Kievan Rus lasted until the Mongols sacked Kyiv in 1240. If you remember it fell in the 1200s after more than three and a half centuries, count back → the late 800s.

groups.label: Event Timeline
items: 862 — Rurik's rule at Novgorod begins (the Primary Chronicle's date)
882 — His successor Oleg takes Kiev and makes it the capital
988 — Vladimir's conversion: Christianity becomes the Rus faith
1240 — The Mongols sack Kyiv, ending the Kievan state's power

groups.label: Look Back
items: Ieyasu won the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600, the round-number year. The emperor made him shogun three years later → 1603.

groups.label: Year of 1603
items: 1603 is also the year Elizabeth I died and James VI of Scotland became James I of England. One island nation got a new dynasty in London, the other a new shogunate in Edo, in the same year.
1603 is the first year of Japan's Edo period, named after Ieyasu's capital, Edo, which is today's Tokyo.

groups.label: Look Ahead
items: Commodore Perry's warships arrived in Edo Bay in 1853, exactly 250 years later. Subtract 250 → 1603.
The Tokugawa shogunate ended with the Meiji Restoration in 1868. It lasted 265 years: 1868 − 265 → 1603.
Not 1605 or 1607: Akbar died in 1605 and Jamestown was founded in 1607. Ieyasu came first, in 1603.

groups.label: Event Timeline
items: 1600 — Victory at Sekigahara
1603 — Named shogun by Emperor Go-Yōzei; rules from Edo
1605 — Hands the title to his son Hidetada but keeps real power
1615 — Siege of Osaka destroys the rival Toyotomi family
1616 — Ieyasu dies
